131.prompt:
Paint ONE image: the background painting for an in-game region map of "Haoma", a region in a whimsical 2D browser game. Size 1520 x 920 pixels (landscape, exactly this ratio; if only fixed ratios are offered, use 16:10). This is the painted landscape that sits UNDER the game's map interface. The game draws its own street lines, names, buttons and markers on top later, so the painting must contain none of them.

VIEW AND FEEL
Seen from directly above, like a painted map: not from a side or three-quarter angle. Trees read as small round canopies or small pointed tops with a soft shadow; no trunks showing. Hills, cliffs and slopes read by their light and shadow. Like a hand-painted miniature diorama, quiet and gentle: muted natural colours, soft shadows, a fine even texture over the ground (like felt or fine brush strokes), and only a little scattered detail. Fewer and smaller features is better than more: most of the land is calm open ground, so thin street lines and small labels drawn on top stay easy to read. Storybook, never grim, never photographic, never neon.

WHAT TO PAINT
One island crowded with tall pointed rock spires. Its shape must follow attachment 02 closely (same outline, same position, same proportions), because the game's streets are fixed to those positions (attachment 03).
- The sea and margins: pale parchment white with faint grey wavy hatching suggesting calm water, all round the island, widest at the top right and down the left side.
- The coast edge: a raised, pale cream rim with a soft shadow below it, like the cut edge of a diorama tile, all round the shore.
- Inside the rim: a flat band of soft sea-green ground, wide on the left and along the top, narrow elsewhere.
- Most of the island: a dense crowd of tall, narrow, pointed rock spires and towers packed close together, in pale blue-grey, frosty sea-green and soft grey; their sunlit tips are almost white and the deep gaps between them are darker teal-grey.
- On the slopes of the spires: many tiny dots of muted red-orange and dark blue, like little dwellings or fungi tucked into the rock.
- The bottom edge: a strip of warm brown earth with small pale pebbles and boulders below the spires.
- Light: soft daylight from the upper left; shadow on the lower-right side of every spire.

STYLE
Match attachment 05: Tiny Speck's own painted plants and scenery for this region (soft painterly shapes, gentle shading, no hard black outlines), but much smaller and simpler, as seen on a map from high above.

DO NOT INCLUDE
No text, letters, numbers or labels of any kind. No roads, paths, lines, grids or street markings. No circles, buttons, pins, arrows, icons, stars or "you are here" markers. No compass, legend, scale bar, border, frame, title or vignette. No people or characters. No UI of any kind.

ATTACHMENTS
01  the original 150 x 91 thumbnail of this region's painting (Tiny Speck, public domain). The colours and the layout to follow.
02  that thumbnail enlarged to 1520 x 920 with no extra detail. Follow its shapes closely: coastlines, cliffs, water, forest and open ground in the same places and proportions; repaint everything with real detail.
03  where the game will draw the streets (dark lines) and region exits (yellow circles), at the same 1520 x 920 scale. For placement only: do NOT paint these lines or circles.
04  a screenshot of how the game shows this map today: a blurry enlargement of the thumbnail with the game's interface drawn on top (street lines, street names, green GO buttons, panel and buttons). It is here only so you can see what the painting is for. Do NOT copy any of the interface; paint only the landscape underneath it.
05  Tiny Speck's own painted trees, plants and scenery from this region's streets (public domain). The style and palette to match, drawn smaller and simpler.

Return the single painted landscape image only.
